Summary: The Second Coming is the promised return of Jesus Christ in glory to judge the living and the dead, defeat evil, and establish God's kingdom in full. Christians live in hopeful readiness, working and praying until He comes.
HistoricalDevelopment: Confessed in the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds from the early centuries, expectation of Christ's return shaped early church hope, medieval theology, and Reformation and modern evangelical teaching.
Interpretations: Christians agree Christ will return personally and visibly, while differing on the timing of the rapture and tribulation and on millennial views, including premillennial, amillennial, and postmillennial readings.
RelatedTopics: Eschatology; Judgment; Millennial Views; Hope; Kingdom of God
